svg.text: Best discriminator level for a signal of N counts/s with an inseparable photon background f*N
A. Dark measured in an off run of equal length
N: signal rate, counts/s at the valley level
photon background fraction f
B. Dark known precisely (separate long dark run)
N: signal rate, counts/s at the valley level
photon background fraction f
best level (one level for all four pairings), mV; GUI value = -level/1000 V
Dashed white: lines of constant N' = N (1 + f). The statistical optimum is exactly the
photon-free one at N', so the level is constant along each. They are nearly vertical: f acts
like a brighter signal, by at most x1.5 at f = 50 %.
C. Dark measured in an off run of equal length
N: signal rate, counts/s at the valley level
best level |v| (mV)
valley 4.0 / 3.8 mV: lowest level scored
f = 0: one level for all four; shaded: within 5 % in all four
f = 0.1: one level for all four; shaded: within 5 % in all four
f = 0.5: one level for all four; shaded: within 5 % in all four
D. Dark known precisely (separate long dark run)
N: signal rate, counts/s at the valley level
best level |v| (mV)
valley 4.0 / 3.8 mV: lowest level scored
f = 0: one level for all four; shaded: within 5 % in all four
f = 0.1: one level for all four; shaded: within 5 % in all four
f = 0.5: one level for all four; shaded: within 5 % in all four
eps(v) from room-light scans (light 13:59, light 17:24); b(v) from the 2026-11-10 dark scans (dark 13:20, dark 16:36), fitted by selftest._smooth_dark_rate. R8486 at ~1000 V
(operator; HV not in the files). The photon background is a MODEL: fraction f of the signal, same pulse heights, absent from the off run.
Statistical optimum only. The systematic error from an uncertain f does not depend on the level, so it does not move the best level; see fig_total_time_vs_level.svg and
fig_flatness_fixed_time.svg for what it does change. Levels are the scanned grid (0.2 mV steps below 6 mV, 0.4 mV above); every level shown is below 10 mV, so valid only with
the cables as they were (manual p. 22).
